info.title: Wardnet API
info.description: Self-hosted network privacy gateway — REST API for device, tunnel, routing, DHCP, DNS, and update management.

post.description: Log in with username and password. On success, sets a `wardnet_session` cookie the browser replays on subsequent admin-gated requests. The JSON body also carries the raw `token` and `expires_in_seconds` so non-browser clients (scripts, the `wctl` CLI, third-party integrations) can replay the token via `Authorization: Bearer <token>` without a cookie jar.

200.description: Login successful; session cookie is set

401.description: Invalid credentials

post.description: End the current session. Deletes the session server-side so the token can never authenticate again, and clears the `wardnet_session` cookie in the response. Requires a valid session cookie or a `Authorization: Bearer <session token>` header; only the session that authenticated this request is affected. Callers authenticated with an API key get a 401 — API keys are not sessions and cannot be logged out here.

401.description: No valid session

403.description: Caller lacks an admin auth context

post.description: Slide the current session's expiry forward by 30 days. Called by the admin-app on every open to implement the 'login once' sliding-window behaviour. Requires a valid session cookie or `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header.

204.description: Session expiry extended; fresh Set-Cookie issued

401.description: No valid session

403.description: Session was not created with remember_me

post.description: Produce an encrypted bundle and stream it back as `application/octet-stream`. The passphrase is required again on restore; the daemon cannot recover a forgotten one.

AddInboundWgPeerRequest.description:
Request body for `POST /api/inbound-wg/peers`.

A remote-access grant targets an already-managed device (issue #810): the
peer's user-facing name is taken from that device, not supplied here.

device_id.description:
The device to grant remote access to. Must already exist (discovered on
the LAN at least once) and must not already have a credential.

AddInboundWgPeerResponse.description:
Response for `POST /api/inbound-wg/peers`.

Carries the complete, ready-to-import `WireGuard` client configuration —
assembled server-side and containing the freshly generated **private key**
exactly once. The daemon never persists the private key (it lives only in
this response); the admin must copy/scan it now. This is the ONLY endpoint
that ever exposes private key material, and it is admin-gated.

allowed_ip.description: The peer's allocated `/32` inside the inbound tunnel subnet.

client_config.description:
The full `WireGuard` client config (`.conf`) — `[Interface]`/`[Peer]`
stanzas including the private key and endpoint — ready to render as a QR
code or download. `None` when no reachable endpoint is known yet (remote
access / DDNS not configured); the credential is created but not usable
until an endpoint exists.

oneOf.description:
Set when transitioning into [`WizardStep::Dhcp`] so the daemon
knows which onboarding branch to take.

AllowedTargetKind.description: A permitted routing-target *kind* a zone allows. Coarse: any tunnel, or direct.

AllowlistEntry.description:
An allowlist entry, scoped to a DNS filter profile, that overrides
blocklist matches.

request_id.description: Request ID for correlation with server logs.

API-layer mirror of [`wardnetd_services::logging::error_notifier::ErrorEntry`] that
carries an `OpenAPI` schema. The service-layer type lives in a crate that does
not depend on `utoipa`; duplicating the small struct here keeps the schema
boundary aligned with the HTTP API without leaking the docs dependency into
the services crate.

ApplyImportRequest.description:
Request body for `POST /api/backup/import/apply`.

Consumes the `preview_token` returned by `/preview`, ensuring the
apply step always has a prior preview (no silent blind restores).

ApplyImportResponse.description:
Response for `POST /api/backup/import/apply`.

Returned once the swap completes. The daemon restarts subsystems
(DHCP/DNS/update runners) after the swap; subsequent API calls see
the restored state.

manifest.description:
Final manifest for the applied bundle — identical to the one
surfaced in the preview but repeated here so the UI can confirm
without re-fetching.

snapshots.description:
`.bak-<timestamp>` snapshots of the files that were replaced.
Retained by the background cleanup task for 24 h.

oneOf.description: Nothing happening. The subsystem is ready to export or import.
Bundle is being packed and encrypted for download.
An import is in progress — `phase` describes where.
The last import failed; the error is retained until the next operation.

BackupStatus.description: Coarse subsystem status surfaced by `GET /api/backup/status` and the web UI.

BestServerSelector.description:
Selector persisted when a tunnel was created via country-scoped auto-select.
Present only on "best server" tunnels; `None` for specific-server or manual.

Blocklist.description: A URL-sourced domain blocklist scoped to a DNS filter profile.

last_error.description:
Error message from the most recent failed download/parse, if any.
Cleared on a successful refresh. Surfaced in the Ad Blocking UI so
users can diagnose blocklist issues without inspecting daemon logs.

last_error_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent failed download/parse.

BundleManifest.description:
Metadata describing a bundle. Serialised as `manifest.json` inside the tar.

The manifest is the first entry extracted during validation so we can
reject incompatible bundles before touching any daemon state.

created_at.description: UTC timestamp the bundle was created.

host_id.description:
Opaque identifier for the source host (hostname or a stable system id).
Surfaced in the restore preview so operators can confirm they're not
restoring a bundle from the wrong machine.

key_count.description:
Number of `WireGuard` key files included in the bundle. Surfaced in the
preview UI so the operator knows exactly what will be overwritten.

schema_version.description: Highest applied sqlx migration version at export time.

wardnet_version.description:
Daemon version (from `WARDNET_VERSION`) that produced the bundle, e.g.
`0.2.0` or `0.2.1-dev.7+gabc1234`. Informational — not used for compat.

ConditionalForwardingRule.description: A conditional forwarding rule (domain → specific upstream).

domain.description: The fully-qualified domain the operator controls, e.g. `home.example.com`.

token.description: A Cloudflare API token scoped to DNS:Edit on the domain's zone.

CountryInfo.description: A country available from a VPN provider.

CreateNetworkZoneRequest.description:
Request body for POST /api/network/zones. `provenance` is forced to `Manual`
server-side; default flags are never set on create (use PUT to promote).

zone_id.description: Optional owning zone. `null`/omitted creates an unzoned record.

resolved_server_name.description: Human-readable name of the server resolved at creation time.

oneOf.description: Set when the tunnel was created via country-scoped auto-select.

CustomFilterRule.description: A user-created AdGuard-syntax filter rule, scoped to a DNS filter profile.

available.description: `true` when the slug is well-formed and unclaimed.

code.description: The one-time code emailed to the account, as entered by the operator.

email.description: The wardnet account email a one-time enrollment code is emailed to.

DdnsRegisterRequest.description: Request body for `POST /api/ddns/register` (wardnet provider, final step).

display_name.description: Optional human-facing network name; defaults to the slug when omitted.

slug.description:
The vanity slug to claim, e.g. `happy-einstein`, forming
`<slug>.my.wardnet.services`. The cloud validates it (3–32 chars,
`[a-z0-9-]`, no leading/trailing hyphen, not reserved).

adopted.description:
`true` when the daemon JOINED an already-existing network of this
account (same slug, re-enrollment) instead of creating a fresh one —
the network's region and name won over the request (display only).

fqdn.description: The public hostname now assigned to this network.

region.description: The region slug (display only); `None` for BYOD-Cloudflare.

expected_ip.description:
The IP the daemon last published (the value public DNS is expected to
return), if any.

fqdn.description: The canonical FQDN that was queried, if DDNS is configured.

resolved_ips.description: The A records the external resolver actually returned for `fqdn`.

DdnsResolutionVerdict.description:
Verdict of the external [resolution check](DdnsResolutionCheckResponse):
whether the *public* internet resolves the canonical FQDN to the IP the
daemon last published. Deliberately bypasses the local split-horizon override.

fqdn.description: The active public hostname (wardnet subdomain or BYOD domain), if any.

last_public_ip.description: The IP last published by the daemon, if any.

provider.description: `None` when DDNS is not configured; otherwise `"wardnet"` or `"cloudflare"`.

suspended.description:
`true` when the wardnet subscription is suspended — the premium app
surfaces (user PWA + admin mobile app) are disabled until it is restored.
Always `false` for BYOD-Cloudflare.

DecideRuleRequestRequest.description:
Request body for `PATCH /api/rule-requests/{id}` (admin decision). Only
`approved` / `rejected` are accepted — a request cannot be set back to
`pending`.

connection_mode.description:
How the device is currently reachable (LAN vs. inbound `WireGuard`).
Live status, last-observation-wins — see [`DeviceConnectionMode`].

zone_id.description:
The Network Zone this device belongs to (exactly one). Sticky: set from
the default-for-new zone at discovery-insert time; never resolved at read
time. See [`crate::network_zone`] and epic #244.

DeviceCaptureToggleRequest.description:
Request body for `PATCH /api/devices/me/dns-capture` — the self-service
capture toggle. Flips only the `enabled` flag; retention caps stay
admin-only (set via `DnsCaptureSettingsRequest` on the admin endpoint).

DeviceConnectionMode.description:
How a device is currently reachable on the network (issue #810).

A **live status**, not a lineage tag: a device flips between the two as it
connects from different paths over time (last-observation-wins), exactly
like `last_ip` already does across DHCP renewals. Set by whichever path
most recently observed the device — LAN ARP/DHCP discovery sets [`Lan`], an
inbound `WireGuard` handshake sets [`Remote`].

[`Lan`]: DeviceConnectionMode::Lan
[`Remote`]: DeviceConnectionMode::Remote

DeviceDnsFilterSettings.description:
Per-device DNS filtering settings.

`enabled = false` is the kill switch; the device's queries skip filtering
entirely. When `enabled = true` and `profile_ids` is empty, the device
inherits the global default profiles from [`DnsFilterConfig`].

profile_ids.description: Explicit profile assignments. Empty means "follow the default profiles".

available_tunnels.description: Available tunnels for self-service routing selection.

oneOf.description:
The caller device's Network Zone, resolved server-side for the
read-only zone display. `None` if the device or its zone can't be
resolved.

DeviceType.description: The type/category of a network device.

DeviceWithStatus.description:
A device enriched with its DHCP status and current routing target for API
responses.

Uses `#[serde(flatten)]` so the JSON output includes all `Device` fields
at the top level alongside `dhcp_status` and `current_rule`, keeping the
response backwards-compatible for consumers that ignore unknown fields.

`current_rule` mirrors [`DeviceDetailResponse::current_rule`]: `None` means
the device has no rule of its own and follows the gateway default policy;
`Some(RoutingTarget::Default)` is an explicit persisted default choice.

DhcpConfig.description:
DHCP pool configuration.

Wardnet IS the gateway and DNS server — no need for users to configure those.
The daemon auto-detects its own LAN IP and advertises itself as gateway (option 3)
and DNS server (option 6) to clients. Option 3 includes the router IP as secondary
entry for automatic failover on supported clients.

gateway_ip.description:
Wardnet's own LAN IP — auto-detected from the LAN interface.
Advertised as gateway (option 3) and DNS server (option 6).

router_ip.description: Fallback router — the real router's IP, included as secondary in option 3.

DhcpLease.description: An active or historical DHCP lease.

DhcpLeaseStatus.description: The current status of a DHCP lease.

DhcpSelfProbeResponse.description:
Response for POST /api/network/dhcp-self-probe.

The wizard's primary-mode step 3 uses this to verify Wardnet now
owns LAN DHCP after the operator disabled it on their router:

- `wardnet_responded == true && foreign_responded == false` → ready
  to advance.
- `foreign_responded == true` → re-show the disable-DHCP guide;
  `foreign_server_ip` lets the wizard call out which device is
  still answering.

DhcpSource.description:
How the LAN interface acquired its current IP address.

Returned by `GET /api/network/status` so the wizard's network step
can show a remediation panel when the host is still relying on
DHCP — install.sh writes `/etc/dhcpcd.conf.d/wardnet.conf` when the
operator passes `--static-ip`, which flips this to `Static`.

DhcpStatus.description: Whether a device's IP is managed by the wardnet DHCP server.

DiscoverGatewayMacRequest.description:
Request body for POST /api/network/discover-gateway-mac.

All fields optional. If `mac` is provided the daemon skips the ARP
probe and just persists the value (validated). Otherwise it probes
the gateway IP from `GET /api/network/status`; `target_ip` lets a
caller override that for testing or when the gateway differs from
the kernel's default route.

DnsConfig.description:
Top-level DNS server configuration.

Persisted as individual keys in the `system_config` KV table,
following the same pattern as [`crate::dhcp::DhcpConfig`].

dns_filtering_enabled.description:
Global DNS filtering emergency stop. When `false`, every query
short-circuits to `Pass` regardless of per-device or per-profile
state — the kill switch above the kill switch.

forwarder_selection_mode.description: How the configured upstreams are used on the forwarding path.

single_upstream.description:
The `address` of the single chosen upstream. `Some` iff
`forwarder_selection_mode` is [`ForwarderSelectionMode::Single`], and
always one of the `upstream_servers` addresses.

default_profile_ids.description:
Profiles applied to devices with no explicit assignment. Empty means
unassigned devices skip filtering. Multiple profiles stack — a domain
blocked in any of them is blocked. Treat as a set: the order across
the get/set roundtrip is not preserved.

enabled.description:
Global emergency stop. When `false`, every query short-circuits to
`Pass` regardless of profile state.

filters_ready.description:
Whether the filters are actually being enforced right now.

The DNS server answers queries as soon as it binds, but the compiled
filters are built in the background — and after an upgrade that resets
the blocklist cache, the lists have to be re-downloaded before they can
block anything. During either window DNS resolves normally and
blocklists are **not** enforced, which is a fail-open the admin has to
be able to see. `false` means exactly that.

pending_blocklists.description:
How many enabled blocklists have never been imported, i.e. are empty and
enforcing nothing until their first download completes.

DnsFilterProfile.description:
A named bundle of DNS filter sources (blocklists, allowlist, custom rules).

Builtin profiles cannot be deleted or modified — the API responds with
`409 Conflict` when an admin attempts either operation.

description.description:
Optional operator-supplied annotation. Builtin profiles carry a
seeded description; custom profiles default to `None`.

DnsProtocol.description: Transport protocol for upstream DNS communication.

DnsQueryLogEntry.description: A single entry in the DNS query log.

DnsQueryResult.description:
Result classification for a DNS query.

Each variant's `snake_case` serialisation exactly matches the string the DNS
resolver writes to the `dns_query_log.result` column, so no translation is
needed between the DB and the API.

DnsRecordSource.description:
Provenance of a custom local DNS record.

`Manual` records are admin-created via the API. `Dhcp` records are
auto-registered by [`crate::event::WardnetEvent::DhcpLeaseAssigned`] /
`DhcpLeaseRenewed` (the `{hostname}.lan` integration). `System` is
reserved for daemon-seeded records that must not be hand-edited.

DnsRecordType.description: DNS record type for custom local records.

upstream_latencies.description:
Rolling-average latency per configured upstream, from the background
prober. One entry per `upstream_servers` address; empty until the
prober has run at least once.

DnsZoneSource.description:
Provenance of an authoritative local DNS zone.

`Manual` zones are admin-created via the API and freely deletable. `System`
zones are daemon-seeded (currently only the `.lan` zone) and **cannot be
deleted** — `DnsLocalService::delete_zone` rejects them. Zones are never
DHCP-sourced, so (unlike [`DnsRecordSource`]) there is no `Dhcp` variant.

ExceptionEndpoint.description:
One side of a cross-zone exception: a `kind`-tagged reference to a device or
a zone.

ExceptionEndpointKind.description:
The kind of endpoint a cross-zone exception references. An endpoint is either
a single device or a whole zone; the `id` is interpreted against the matching
catalog (`devices` or `network_zones`). FKs are soft/kind-tagged and are
validated in the service, not the schema.

ExportBackupRequest.description:
Request body for `POST /api/backup/export`.

The passphrase is used to derive the age encryption key via scrypt.
Server-side we enforce a minimum length of
`crate::backup::MIN_PASSPHRASE_LEN`; clients should surface the same
minimum in UI copy so failures happen before the request.

passphrase.description:
Passphrase chosen by the admin. Never logged, never persisted —
lives only in the memory of the request that produced the bundle.

ForwarderSelectionMode.description:
How the configured upstreams are used on the forwarding path
(only meaningful in [`DnsResolutionMode::Forwarding`]).

HealthComponentDto.description: One component's debounced status within a [`HealthResponse`].

detail.description: Failure detail, present only while the component is `DOWN`.

HealthResponse.description:
Response body for `GET /health` (issue #214).

Unauthenticated, Actuator/k8s-style. The HTTP status code carries the
machine-readable verdict (200 UP / 503 DOWN); the body adds the per-
component breakdown for humans and dashboards.

status.description: Overall verdict — `DOWN` if any component is down.

HealthStatusDto.description:
Overall health verdict surfaced by `GET /health` (issue #214).

Maps to the HTTP status: `Up` → 200, `Down` → 503. Mirrors the
`HealthStatus` produced by the daemon's `HealthMonitor`.

enabled.description: Whether the inbound `WireGuard` server should be running.

listen_port.description: UDP port the server listens on for inbound peer handshakes.

server_public_key.description:
The server's public key once a keypair exists (generated on first
enable). `None` until the server has been enabled at least once.

InboundWgPeerSummary.description: A single inbound-`WireGuard` peer, without any private key material.

device_id.description:
The `Device` this credential grants remote access to. `None` only for
pre-#810 rows written before the device link existed; every row
written since always carries it.

InfoResponse.description:
Response from the public info endpoint.

Returns basic server information without requiring authentication.
Used by the web UI's connection status widget.

entitled.description:
Whether this box is currently entitled to the premium app surfaces
(the user PWA and admin mobile app) — on the wardnet DDNS provider and
not suspended. The web UI uses this to self-gate an already-installed
PWA served from its service-worker precache, which never re-hits the
server-side serving gate.

release_version.description:
Public-facing `CalVer` (`YYYY.MM.DD`) read from the workspace-
root `CALVER` file at compile time. Stable across dev rebuilds
and is the string the web UI displays, the auto-update runner
compares against the published manifest, and the `OpenAPI` spec
declares as `info.version`.

version.description:
Diagnostic version string — git-derived
`MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH[-dev.N+gHASH]`. Carries dev-suffix on
non-tag builds so logs and `--version` output identify the
exact commit. Use `release_version` for anything user-facing.

InstallHandle.description: Handle returned when an install is kicked off.

oneOf.description: No install in progress.
Resolving the manifest for the target channel.
Downloading the release tarball.
Verifying SHA-256 and (if enabled) minisign signature.
Extracting and staging the binary on disk.
Atomically swapping the binary.
Swap completed, daemon will restart now.
The new binary is running; clearing pending marker.
Install failed — message contains the reason.

InstallPhase.description: Phase of an in-flight update install.

InstallUpdateRequest.description:
Request body for POST /api/update/install.

If `version` is omitted, installs the latest known version for the current
channel. The operation is idempotent — calling twice while one is in
flight returns the same handle.

Job.description: Snapshot of a job, returned by `GET /api/jobs/:id`.

percentage_done.description: Completion percentage, 0..=100. Jumps to 100 when the job terminates.

JobDispatchedResponse.description:
Response body for a handler that dispatches a background job instead of
doing the work inline. The HTTP status code is `202 Accepted`.

JobKind.description:
Discriminator for what kind of work a job represents. The kind is fixed
at job creation time; new kinds get new variants here.

JobStatus.description:
Lifecycle state of a [`Job`]. Jobs start as `Pending`, move to `Running`
when execution begins, and end in one of the two terminal states.

LastShutdownState.description: How the previous daemon shutdown ended.

LastShutdownStatus.description:
Classification of the previous daemon shutdown.

`at` is the timestamp the previous run last touched the database
(graceful exit time, or last heartbeat for unclean events). It is
`None` only for `unknown` (first-ever boot). `acknowledged_at` is
set by `POST /api/system/shutdown/acknowledge`; the banner is
considered dismissed iff `acknowledged_at >= at`.

credentials.description: Credentials for authenticating with the provider.

filter.description: Optional filters for the server list.

servers.description: List of available servers from the provider.

LocalSnapshot.description:
Summary of a local `.bak-*` directory left behind by a previous import.

Retained for 24h by the background cleanup task so operators can manually
recover from a bad restore. Surfaced by `GET /api/backup/snapshots`.

kind.description:
Which file the snapshot was taken of (`"database"`, `"config"`,
`"keys"`). Lets the UI group snapshots produced by the same import.

size_bytes.description: Total size on disk in bytes (directories are summed recursively).

remember_me.description:
When `true`, the session cookie is set with a 30-day `Max-Age` instead
of the default 24-hour expiry. Admin-app always sends `true`; admin-site
exposes this as a "Remember me" checkbox.

LoginResponse.description:
Login response body.

`token` is the same opaque value written into the `wardnet_session` cookie;
non-browser clients (e.g. scripts that don't maintain a cookie jar) can
replay it on admin-gated requests via the `Authorization: Bearer <token>`
header. `expires_in_seconds` is the token's remaining lifetime measured
from the moment this response was generated.

router_mac.description:
Upstream router MAC persisted by the wizard's discover step, if
any — lets the review step display it without re-probing.

NetworkZone.description:
A Network Zone: a named policy bucket a device belongs to (exactly one) that
gates the device's allowed routing targets, its reachability of the Pi's
admin surfaces, and (Phase 2+) its network isolation. See epic #244 and the
`adr-network-zone-isolation` ADR.

admin_ui_reachable.description: May devices in this zone reach the Pi's admin surfaces? (intent-only in Phase 1)

allowed_targets.description: Routing-target kinds a device in this zone may pick. Empty is rejected on write.

is_default.description: The protected "home"/anchor zone. Exactly one true. Deletion-guarded.

is_default_for_new.description: Where freshly-discovered devices are assigned. Exactly one true.

member_isolation.description: Within an isolate-members zone, also isolate same-zone peers. (CI-3 #737)

oneOf.description: Per-zone subnet (CI-3 #737). None for all seeds.

member_count.description: Number of devices currently assigned to this zone.

NetworkZoneView.description:
A Network Zone plus its current member count. Enriched view returned by the
zone list/detail endpoints.

NotificationItem.description:
One entry of the admin notification feed (issue #482): a persisted record
of an admin-audience push notification.

subject_id.description:
Identifier of the subject entity; what it identifies is driven by
`kind` (device UUID for device kinds, tunnel UUID for tunnel kinds).

url.description: App-relative deep link (no PWA base path), e.g. `/devices`.

PortSpec.description:
An inclusive port range for a single protocol. A single port is expressed as
`from == to`.

PreviewDhcpConfigRequest.description:
Request body for POST /api/dhcp/config/preview.

A dry-run that reports which active leases would be revoked if the pool
were changed to `pool_start`–`pool_end`, so the admin can be warned before
saving. Mutates nothing.

affected.description:
Active leases whose IP would fall outside the proposed pool and are not
pinned by a reservation. These devices would be forced to re-acquire an
in-range lease on their next renewal.

ProviderAuthMethod.description: Supported authentication methods for a VPN provider.

oneOf.description: Username/password pair (service credentials).
Access token.

ProviderCredentials.description: Credentials submitted by the admin for provider operations.

ProviderInfo.description: Metadata about a registered VPN provider.

credentials_hint.description: Hint text explaining where to find credentials (shown in the UI).

icon_url.description: URL to the provider's icon/logo for UI display.

PushSubscriptionResponse.description: Response of the push subscription mutation endpoints.

enabled.description: Whether new-device quarantine is on. Off by default.

ok.description: Always `true` on a 200 response. Errors surface as non-200 status codes.

oneOf.description: No restore in progress.
Decrypting the bundle and parsing the manifest.
Stopping DHCP/DNS/update runners so the DB swap is safe.

Renaming current `wardnet.db` / `wardnet.toml` / `keys/` to
`.bak-<timestamp>` siblings.
Extracting bundle contents into place.

Running `sqlx migrate` against the restored database so a
lower-schema-version bundle lands cleanly on a newer daemon.
Restarting runners with the new state.

Something went wrong — the `.bak-*` siblings are still on disk for
manual recovery. `reason` holds the operator-facing error message.

failed.description:
Something went wrong — the `.bak-*` siblings are still on disk for
manual recovery. `reason` holds the operator-facing error message.

RestorePhase.description:
Phase of an in-flight restore. Emitted as progress events so the UI can
show a spinner with meaningful status text.

The restore pipeline is strictly sequential — no phase is ever skipped on
the happy path, and a failure preserves the phase it occurred in so the
operator can tell *where* the restore broke.

RestorePreviewRequest.description:
Schema-only stand-in so the `OpenAPI` spec can describe the
multipart fields `preview_import` accepts. The handler itself
pulls fields out of [`axum::extract::Multipart`] directly — this
type is never materialised at runtime.

passphrase.description: Passphrase that was used to encrypt the bundle on export.

RestorePreviewResponse.description:
Response for `POST /api/backup/import/preview`.

Returned before any daemon state is touched. The UI uses this to show
the admin what will change — which database, config, and key files get
swapped, and which bundle they came from — so the actual apply step
is a conscious confirmation.

compatible.description:
True when the bundle's `bundle_format_version` and
`schema_version` are both compatible with the running daemon. A
`false` here means `apply_import` will refuse; the UI should
surface `incompatibility_reason` and hide the confirm button.

files_to_replace.description:
Files the apply step will rename to `.bak-<timestamp>` siblings
and then overwrite. Surfaced verbatim in the UI so operators
understand the blast radius before confirming.

incompatibility_reason.description:
Human-readable reason the bundle is incompatible, when
`compatible` is `false`. `None` on the happy path.

manifest.description: Bundle manifest, fully decrypted and validated.

preview_token.description:
Opaque token the caller passes back to `apply_import` to prove
they just saw this preview. Scoped to a single bundle + session.

RouterMacSource.description: How the upstream router MAC was obtained.

RoutingTarget.description: Where traffic for a device should be routed.

RuleRequestKind.description: What the user is asking for.

ServerInfo.description: Information about a single VPN server.

ServiceSet.description:
A named, curated bundle of ports for a common cross-zone use case. Presets
keep the wire format compact and let the daemon evolve the underlying ports
without a data migration.

oneOf.description: A named preset (e.g. `casting`).
An explicit list of port specs.

ServiceSpec.description:
How the allowed ports of an exception are specified: either a curated preset
or an explicit list. Internally tagged on the wire so the two shapes are
distinguishable without a discriminant field colliding with payload keys.

SetDefaultPolicyRequest.description:
Request body for PUT /api/system/default-policy.

`policy` is either the literal string `"direct"` or a tunnel UUID.
The service layer validates the format and rejects anything else.

SetInboundWgPeerEnabledRequest.description:
Request body for `PATCH /api/inbound-wg/peers/{id}`.

Pauses or resumes a peer without deleting its credential — distinct from
`DELETE`, which revokes it permanently and requires a fresh keypair (and
QR scan) to re-grant.

credentials.description: Credentials for authenticating with the provider.

hostname.description:
Direct server hostname for dedicated IP or manual server selection.
Bypasses server listing -- resolves directly by hostname.
Accepts short form (`pt131`) or full (`pt131.nordvpn.com`).
Takes precedence over `server_id` when both are set.

label.description: Optional label override; defaults to provider-generated label.

server_id.description: If set, use this specific server ID instead of auto-selecting.

setup_completed.description:
Derived: `wizard_step == Completed`. Kept for `SetupGuard`
backwards-compat — clients that haven't been updated still get a
boolean they understand.

oneOf.description: `None` until step 3 picks a branch.

SnapshotKind.description: What a [`LocalSnapshot`] is a snapshot of.

StatsQueryResponse.description:
Response for a time-series stats query.

The shape of the response mirrors the request: a single-metric
query returns `metric` + `series`; a multi-metric query returns
`results` (metric name → series). Exactly one variant is populated.

StatsSeriesPoint.description: A single point in a stats time series.

labels.description: Sorted JSON labels object for this data point.

StatsTopEntry.description: A single entry in a top-N result.

labels.description: Sorted JSON labels object for this entry.

StatsTopResponse.description: Response for a top-N stats query.

last_shutdown.description:
Classification of the previous daemon shutdown plus its
acknowledgement timestamp. The web UI uses this to surface a
persistent banner after an unclean shutdown until an admin
dismisses it.

TlsProvisioningPhase.description:
Coarse stage of the daemon's TLS-certificate provisioning, surfaced so the
setup wizard and dashboard can show live progress without instrumenting the
ACME round-trip. Persisted in `system_config`, so it survives a restart.

domain.description: The domain being (or already) provisioned, if any.

error.description:
Human-readable error from the last failed attempt, when `phase` is
[`TlsProvisioningPhase::Failed`].

not_after.description: RFC 3339 expiry of the stored certificate, when one has been issued.

Tunnel.description: A `WireGuard` tunnel configuration and its live state.

endpoint_resolved_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the last endpoint re-resolution.

override_default_dns.description:
When `true`, devices routed through this tunnel resolve DNS via
wardnet's DNS server (so the ad-blocking filter still runs) and
wardnet forwards those queries to the tunnel's DNS server with
`SO_BINDTODEVICE`. When `false`, the per-tunnel DNS server (if
any) is ignored and the system-wide upstream pool is used.

resolved_server_name.description: Human-readable name of the last resolved server (e.g. "United States #8395").

oneOf.description:
Set when the tunnel was created via country-scoped auto-select ("best server").
`None` for specific-server or manually imported tunnels.

TunnelDevicesResponse.description:
Response for `GET /api/tunnels/{id}/devices`.

The devices currently routed through the given tunnel — i.e. those
whose user-set or admin-set routing rule has
`target = Tunnel { tunnel_id: id }`.

TunnelSpeedTestHistoryResponse.description: History of recent speed tests for one tunnel, newest first.

TunnelSpeedTestResult.description:
One completed speed test: the direct (WAN) baseline and the tunnel result,
measured back-to-back in a single run.

direct_jitter_ms.description: Latency jitter (sample standard deviation) over the direct path, in ms.

direct_latency_ms.description: Median ICMP round-trip latency over the direct path, in milliseconds.

direct_throughput_mbps.description: Download throughput over the direct (unbound/WAN) path, in megabits/s.

tunnel_jitter_ms.description: Latency jitter (sample standard deviation) through the tunnel, in ms.

tunnel_latency_ms.description: Median ICMP round-trip latency through the tunnel, in milliseconds.

tunnel_throughput_mbps.description: Download throughput through the tunnel interface, in megabits/s.

TunnelStatus.description:
The current status of a `WireGuard` tunnel.

State machine driven by user/admin actions and the tunnel monitor's
health-check loop:

- `Down` — kernel interface not configured (initial state, after
  tear-down, or after delete).
- `Connecting` — `bring_up` succeeded; kernel interface is configured;
  no handshake observed yet.
- `Up` — recent (≤ 3 min) handshake observed.
- `Reconnecting` — was `Up`, last handshake stale (> 3 min) or absent;
  the iface is still configured and `WireGuard` keepalive is retrying.

TunnelSummary.description: Minimal tunnel info exposed to self-service users for routing selection.

TunnelTestResult.description:
Result payload of `POST /api/tunnels/{id}/test`.

The daemon brings the tunnel up if needed, sends a single HTTP probe
through the tunnel interface, and reports the exit IP, ISO-3166 alpha-2
country code, and round-trip latency in milliseconds.

country_code.description: ISO-3166 alpha-2 country code reported by the probe service.

exit_ip.description: Public IP observed at the tunnel exit.

latency_ms.description: Round-trip latency of the probe call, in milliseconds.

UpdateChannel.description:
Update release channel, in ascending order of risk.

`Stable` tracks only full releases (e.g. `2026.07.00`). `Beta` also
considers `-beta.N` pre-releases, which are still cut through the full
release ceremony. `Edge` follows `-edge.N` builds published straight from
a branch with no review and no test gates — an operator's testing loop,
never a destination for a real user. Edge is gated by the deploy-time
`[update] allow_edge_channel` flag; the service layer rejects it unless
that flag is set. See `docs/adr/0023-edge-release-channel.md`.

admin_locked.description: Whether to lock routing changes for this device.

oneOf.description: Routing target to set for this device (admin bypasses lock check).

single_upstream.description:
The chosen single upstream's `address`. Only consulted when the
resulting mode is `single`; ignored (and forced clear) in the other
modes. Omit to leave the current selection unchanged.

UpdateDnsFilterConfigRequest.description:
Request body for PUT /api/dns/filter/config.

Both fields are partial-update: omitted from JSON = no change. For
`default_profile_ids`, an empty list clears the default (unassigned
devices stop being filtered) and a non-empty list replaces the entire
set.

UpdateHistoryEntry.description: A single entry in the persistent update history.

UpdateHistoryStatus.description: Final status of a historical update attempt.

UpdateNetworkZoneRequest.description:
Request body for PUT /api/network/zones/{id} (partial update). Every field
is optional. `is_default`/`is_default_for_new` set to `Some(true)` promote
this zone to the anchor / default-for-new; `Some(false)` is rejected (flags
only move by promoting another zone). `subnet: Some(None)` clears the subnet.

UpdateProfileRequest.description:
Request body for PUT /api/dns/filter/profiles/{id}.

All fields are partial-update: omitting them from JSON leaves the stored
value unchanged. Pass `description: null` to clear an existing description.

description.description:
`undefined` / omitted = leave unchanged. `null` = clear. `string` = set.

Standard serde cannot distinguish "field absent" from "field: null" for
`Option<T>`. The custom deserializer below wraps the inner deserialize so
that `null` → `Some(None)` and absent → `None`, giving us three states.

zone_id.description:
Three-state: omitted = leave zone link unchanged, `null` = clear to
NULL (unzoned), value = reassign. See [`crate::serde_util::nullable_field`].

UpdateStatus.description: Snapshot of the update subsystem's current state.

applied_at.description:
When `applied_version` was observed running. Clients dedupe their
"updated to vX" notification on this timestamp.

applied_version.description:
Version the daemon most recently *finished* applying across a restart.

Set by the startup reconcile when `pending_version` matched the running
binary. The UI polls status and has no event channel, so this (paired
with `applied_at`) is how a browser learns an update landed.

edge_available.description:
Whether this box may follow the `edge` channel — i.e. whether
`[update] allow_edge_channel` is set in `/etc/wardnet/wardnet.toml`.

Setting it requires root *on the box*, so the UI cannot enable edge
itself; it only renders the option when the daemon says it exists.

last_check_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of the last successful check, if any.

last_install_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of the most recent install attempt.

latest_version.description: Latest version known for the active channel (if any check has run).

pending_version.description:
Version the in-flight install is targeting (if any).

Cleared by the startup reconcile once the daemon comes back up on the
new binary — a pending version that outlives the restart would other-
wise be reported forever.

rollback_available.description: Whether a `.old` binary is present that could be rolled back to.

update_available.description: Whether a newer version than the running one is available.

override_default_dns.description:
`true` routes tunneled-device DNS through wardnet (so the
ad-blocking filter still runs) using the tunnel's DNS server as
upstream with `SO_BINDTODEVICE`. `false` falls back to the
system-wide upstream pool. See issue #342.

UpdateZoneExceptionRequest.description:
Request body for PUT /api/network/zones/exceptions/{id} (partial update).
Every field is optional; absent fields are left unchanged.

port.description: Port (default: 53 for UDP/TCP, 853 for TLS, 443 for HTTPS).

tls_server_name.description:
TLS server name (SNI) for DoT/DoH. Required when `protocol` is
`Tls`/`Https`, ignored otherwise: `address` is the IP to dial, and
this is the hostname the upstream's certificate must match (e.g.
address `"1.1.1.1"`, `tls_server_name` `"cloudflare-dns.com"`).

UpstreamDnsRequest.description: Upstream DNS server in API requests.

tls_server_name.description: TLS server name (SNI) — required when protocol is tls/https.

UpstreamLatency.description:
Rolling-average latency telemetry for one configured upstream, produced by
the background latency prober and surfaced in the DNS status response so the
UI can show per-server performance. Not persisted.

avg_latency_ms.description:
Rolling-average round-trip time in milliseconds, or `None` until the
first successful probe.

reachable.description: Whether the most recent probe reached the upstream.

credentials.description: Credentials to validate against the provider.

key.description:
Base64url (unpadded) uncompressed P-256 application server key, passed
to `PushManager.subscribe({ applicationServerKey })` in the browser.

WebPushKeys.description: The subscriber's encryption keys, carried inside [`WebPushSubscription`].

p256dh.description: Base64url (unpadded) P-256 ECDH public key of the subscriber (`p256dh`).

WebPushSubscription.description:
Standard Web Push subscription object as produced in-browser by
`PushManager.subscribe()`. Body of `POST /api/push/subscriptions`.

endpoint.description: Push service endpoint the daemon POSTs encrypted payloads to.

WizardMode.description:
Branch of the DHCP onboarding flow chosen at step 3.

`Primary` runs Wardnet's built-in DHCP server. `LockedRouter` keeps the
upstream ISP router as the LAN's DHCP server and configures opted-in
devices statically with Wardnet as their gateway/DNS.

WizardStep.description:
Linear stage in the first-run setup wizard.

The wizard advances `Admin → Network → Dhcp → RouterMac → Dns → Tunnel →
Policy → RemoteAccess → Review → Completed`. `setup_completed` (in
[`SetupStatusResponse`] and the `SetupGuard` redirect logic) is derived
from `wizard_step == Completed`, so existing installs that already
finished setup are not re-routed through the new wizard after an upgrade.

The wizard may also rewind: any step down to [`Self::Network`] can be
revisited (never [`Self::Admin`] — admin creation is one-shot), except
once [`Self::Completed`] is reached, which is terminal.

Steps are persisted by their stable storage string (not their ordinal), so
inserting [`Self::Dns`] and [`Self::Review`] mid-sequence needs no
migration: finished installs (`"completed"`) and in-progress ones keep
resolving to the same variant.

ZoneException.description:
A cross-zone exception: an admin-granted allowance for one endpoint to reach
another across an otherwise-isolated zone boundary (e.g. a phone casting to a
TV). This is data-model only in issue #737 commit 1; the zone enforcer
consumes it in a later commit.

bidirectional.description:
Whether the allowance applies in both directions (`from ↔ to`) or only
`from → to`.

ZoneProvenance.description:
Whether a zone was seeded by the daemon or created by an admin.
Mirrors the existing DNS "Zone provenance" (system | manual).

ZoneStance.description:
Cross-zone isolation rung of the guarantee ladder (epic #244). Only the rungs
we have issues for exist; VLAN is a documented non-goal (ADR), not a variant.

ZoneSubnet.description: A per-zone subnet (Phase 2 / DHCP-mode). Recorded-only in #735; always None on seeds.

cidr.description: CIDR, e.g. "10.44.0.0/24". Validated when set; unused by any Phase-1 code path.

ZoneSummary.description:
Minimal Network Zone info exposed to a self-service caller for the
read-only zone display in the user PWA.

The caller is device-keyed and has no admin session, so it cannot call the
admin-gated `GET /api/network/zones`. `GET /api/devices/me` resolves the
caller's own zone (via an internal admin context) and hands back just the
name plus whether it is the anchor "home" zone — enough for
"You're on: Guest — isolated from the home network" without leaking the
full zone policy.

is_default.description:
Whether this is the protected anchor "home" zone. When `false` the
device sits in a non-home zone that is isolated from it.
